- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. - simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). # Mathematical working context (C66-GEO-COMP)

Treat candidates as unproved. Reprove every fact used in the final argument. Constraints below are hard stops: do not walk them again.

## Frontier obligations

- The exact monodromy image inside the wreath product S_2 wr S_3 on a type-(ii) fibre, and therefore the S_6-isotypic decomposition of cohomology of the ordering cover on a purely type-(ii) component.
- Whether a connected component of a balanced+(CE)+(N) base can consist entirely of type-(ii) fibres, equivalently whether the type-(i) hypothesis in the family monodromy statement is automatic.
- Whether a non-primitive degree-four pencil factoring through an intermediate curve of genus two or three can satisfy (BAL); if such a cover is balanced, degree reasons force it to be of type (i).
- Extension of the family, Abel-Jacobi, and ordering-torsor statements from reduced locally Noetherian schemes to algebraic stacks with inertia (or to a smooth atlas with descent of the identification AJ=P(pi_* L)) and to nonreduced bases, where Grauert local freeness and constant-rank cohomology need a separate lifting argument.
- The H_alpha-object given by ordinary or Borel-Moore cohomology of a connected component of the ordering cover, as a mixed Hodge structure; the induction isomorphism does not determine Tate type of that object.
- A stack-level identification of Aut groups for the Abel-Jacobi incidence versus Aut(C,gamma,Gamma), and the existence, representability, unramifiedness, quasi-finiteness, and image-closure properties of a morphism from the balanced ordered model to M_{6,6}.
- Characteristic-zero reflexivity/biduality for a reduced irreducible plane curve (birationality of the Gauss map onto the dual curve) and Jordan's theorem that a primitive subgroup of S_n containing a transposition is S_n, if these are used as inputs rather than independently established.
- Irreducibility of the balanced base of the family, and consequently the number of irreducible components of the ordered evaluation-failure locus, are undetermined; the component correspondence only transports components of the base to components of the incidence and its distinct-support open.

## Mathematical constraints

- Connectedness of the finite etale right S_6-torsor Ord(|L|^{rs})->|L|^{rs} is equivalent to transitivity of the monodromy image G on the six points of a general divisor. [reason: Transitivity of G on six letters means G acts transitively on the standard set {1,...,6}, which already holds for A_6. For a right S_6-torsor the connected components are indexed by the orbit set H\S_6 of left multiplication, so connectedness is equivalent to H=S_6 (a single right coset), not to transitivity. Since [S_6:A_6]=2, an A_6 image would give two connected components.]
- The set of orbits of left multiplication by a monodromy image H on S_6 may be named 'left cosets H\S_6', and the right deck action may then be written on symbols gH with component stabilizer gHg^{-1}. [reason: The orbits of left multiplication of H on G are the right cosets Hg; the set of those orbits is H\G. Genuine left cosets are gH, and right multiplication on G/H={gH} is well-defined if and only if H is normal in G. The stabilizer of the component indexed by Hg is g^{-1}Hg, not gHg^{-1}, unless H is normal.]
- Identifying the relative degree-six linear system with Proj(pi_*L) over an arbitrary base. [reason: Where h^0(L) jumps, pi_*L does not commute with base change and Proj(pi_*L) has the wrong fibres; the construction is valid only over the open locus of constant h^0. The base-independent model is the Abel-Jacobi incidence Sym^6(C/B) x_{Pic^6(C/B)} B, closed by separatedness of the relative Picard scheme, and it agrees with Proj(pi_*L) only over that open.]
- Deducing a global direct-sum splitting W ~= W_4 + W_5 from fibrewise balancedness F_s ~= O(4) + O(5). [reason: Fibrewise balancedness only supplies the relative Harder-Narasimhan filtration 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0. A global splitting is an extra hypothesis: its obstruction is the extension class in Ext^1_{P^1_B}(L_4, L_5), which lies in H^1(B, gamma'_*O(1)) and need not vanish over a general base, while the fibrewise Ext vanishes so no local obstruction is visible.]
- Inferring exactness of pi_* on the filtration 0 -> W_4 -> W -> W_5 -> 0 from finiteness of Gamma over the base. [reason: Finiteness of Gamma gives only exactness of restriction to Gamma (the sequence is locally split, so it survives tensoring with O_Gamma) and exactness of pushforward along Gamma -> B. Surjectivity of pi_*W -> pi_*W_5 along the curve fibration is a separate vanishing statement R^1 pi_* W_4 = 0, which must be certified by a degree inequality deg W_4 > 2g-2 and rechecked whenever deg W_4 <= 2g-2.]
- Concluding local freeness of pi_*L and R^1 pi_*L, and arbitrary base change, from constancy of the fibre dimensions on geometric points over an arbitrary base. [reason: Grauert's criterion requires the base to be reduced. Over a nonreduced base, constant dimensions of the cohomology of a perfect two-term complex on geometric fibres do not imply locally free cohomology; a separate scheme-theoretic constant-rank or lifting argument is required.]
- Deriving a local complete intersection or regular-immersion conclusion from a comparison between the actual codimension of a degeneracy locus and the generic determinantal expected codimension. [reason: Expected-codimension bookkeeping is neither necessary nor sufficient for regularity: a component of codimension below the determinantal expectation may still be locally cut out by a regular sequence of its actual codimension, and a nowhere-lci conclusion requires local ideal-depth or conormal calculations. The valid route is a closed immersion between schemes smooth over the base, whose codimension is the relative-dimension difference.]
- Treating the balanced reduced-support relative linear system as a closed pure-codimension-four subvariety of M_{6,6} and applying a Gysin morphism to the pair. [reason: The balanced reduced-support model is only an open piece of the evaluation-failure locus; Gysin for (M_{6,6}, Z) requires a closed (stratified) embedding obtained after h^0 and splitting-type stratification. Openness of balancedness inside the tetragonal locus supplies neither closedness nor purity.]
- Asserting that the balanced CE failure model maps monomorphically into an evaluation-failure locus in M_{6,6} while disclaiming the identification L ~= omega_C(-D). [reason: M_{6,6} forgets the pencil gamma, and a general genus-6 curve carries five distinct g^1_4's, so the underlying forgetful map is generically five-to-one; injectivity requires recovering gamma from L, whose only standard route is L ~= omega_C(-D), returning the pencil as |omega_C tensor L^{-1}|. Additionally, CE failure is a condition on the pair (C, gamma), not on a point of M_{6,6}, so the target of the claimed monomorphism is not well-defined without a stack-level full-faithfulness argument.]
- Passing from the ordered configuration model to the unordered divisor model by reducing only the source, i.e. forming I_red -> I^{red-supp}. [reason: The canonical torsor is I -> I^{red-supp} and its reduced form is I_red -> (I^{red-supp})_red; reducing only the source generally destroys flatness over nonreduced bases, so the finite etale torsor property is lost.]
- Upgrading the count of pi_1^etale-orbits (connected components of the finite etale S_6-cover) to a count of irreducible components without a normality hypothesis on the base. [reason: A connected finite etale cover of a connected locally Noetherian base need not be irreducible; connectedness and irreducibility diverge on non-normal bases, so the [S_6 : H] component formula requires normality or an independent geometric-irreducibility argument.]
- Proving a stabilizer or inertia clause by observing that an automorphism induces a PGL_2 transformation of P^1 fixing the marked images, and then quoting the clause for the forgetful map to M_{6,6}. [reason: That argument computes Aut(C, gamma, Gamma), automorphisms of the tetragonal cover preserving the divisor, whereas the group relevant to M_{6,6} is Aut(C, Gamma). An automorphism of C preserving Gamma need not preserve the pencil, and triviality of the kernel is not formal, since a nontrivial automorphism of a genus-6 curve can fix as many as 2g+2 = 14 points and hence can fix six marked points.]
- Identifying the excess cokernel along the ordered etale incidence over the projective bundle with the pullback of R^1 pi_* L without a twist. [reason: The cokernel is globally the pullback of R^1 pi_* L tensored by the convention-dependent tautological line M_univ determined by O(D_univ) = L tensor pi^*M_univ; the fibrewise isomorphism with H^1(L_b) requires a choice of trivialization of the one-dimensional M_univ fibre and does not yield an untwisted Hodge-bundle isomorphism, so excess and Chern-class computations must retain the line twist or prove it trivial.]
- Using a single stratum dimension for every stratum in the formula dim(I|_{H_k}) = dim(H_k) + k - 1. [reason: The formula is stratum-dependent; substituting one fixed value of dim(H_k) across all strata contradicts the separately established bound on the deeper stratum's dimension, so the resulting dimension estimates are internally inconsistent.]
- Concluding that a forgetful morphism has finite fibres or is quasi-finite from injectivity over one stratum together with a bound on fibre dimension over another. [reason: A positive bound on fibre dimension over a stratum is compatible with positive-dimensional fibres there; quasi-finiteness requires zero-dimensional fibres over every point, and stratum-by-stratum statements of mixed strength do not assemble into a global finiteness statement.]
- Concluding pure-Tate cohomology of the failure locus from rationality of the irreducible representations of S_6 or from a finite branch morphism of the Hurwitz stack to an open of a moduli of pointed rational curves. [reason: Rational irreducibility of the representations of the deck group does not constrain the geometric monodromy of the tetragonal family or the configuration-space coefficients, and a finite pushforward of the constant sheaf may contain non-Tate local systems; rational averaging preserves an already established Tate structure but cannot create one.]

[reason: The identification of O_{P(E^vee)}(2)|_C tensor gamma^*O(-6) with A^6 uses omega_C = A^5 together with O_{P(E^vee)}(1)|_C = omega_{C/P^1}, i.e. exactly the normalization being disclaimed; the stated independence is therefore not supported by that route. A normalization-free count exists but is a different argument: deg = 36 - 24 = 12 > 2g-2 = 10 gives h^1 = 0 and h^0 = 7 by Riemann-Roch whatever the line bundle is.]

[evidence: mechanical; Arithmetic receipt: deg L = deg W_5 - (2g-2) = 16 - 10 = 6; chi(L) = 6 - 6 + 1 = 1; Clifford bound deg(D)/2 + 1 = 4/2 + 1 = 3; cross-check deg(omega_C^2(-D)) = 2*10 - 4 = 16 = deg W_5 at g=6, f=5.]
